title: What Is a Church Elder, and Why More Than One?
subtitle: The New Testament gives the church a plurality of shepherds for a reason, and the reason protects everyone, the pastor most of all.

sections.title: What the New Testament Actually Asks
sections.body:
Start where the Bible starts, which is character, almost entirely. Read First Timothy three and Titus one and notice how little is said about skill and how much is said about a life. Above reproach. Faithful to one wife. Temperate, self-controlled, hospitable, able to teach. Not violent but gentle. Not quarrelsome. Not a lover of money. Manages his own household well.

One competency is named, the ability to teach, and even it is set inside a long list of character. The office is not handed to the impressive. It is handed to the proven. The qualification is a tested life, watched over time by people who know the man at home and not only at church.

And notice the words for the office overlap. Elder, overseer, shepherd, all describe the same role from three angles. The elder is the older, proven man. The overseer watches and guards. The shepherd feeds and protects and goes after the one that strays. One office, three pictures, and every picture is about caring for people rather than running an organization.

sections.title: How to Find One, and How Not To
sections.body:
Most churches identify elders the wrong way, and I have done it the wrong way myself. We look for the successful businessman, the man with influence, the one who can read a budget and command a room. We are choosing a board, so we recruit directors, and then we wonder why the elders govern the church like a company and shepherd no one.

Scripture does not describe a board. It describes shepherds. So look for the men already doing the work without the title. The one who visits the sick because he cannot help it. The one young men gather around. The one who has quietly walked a family through a death and never mentioned it. The man who is an elder in everything but name is the man to name, because the office should confirm a calling already visible, not create one that is not there.

The concrete practice is patience. Watch a man for years, not months. Watch his marriage, his children, his temper, his money, his response to correction. First Timothy says do not be hasty in laying on hands, and the haste is exactly the sin a growing church commits, lifting men into the office before their character has been tested, then living with the consequences for a decade.

sections.title: Why Plurality Protects Everyone
sections.body:
The New Testament never describes a church run by one man. It describes elders, plural, in every city, in every letter. This is not an accident of culture. It is a protection, and the first person it protects is the pastor.

A man alone at the top is a man unaccountable, unguarded, and unbearably exposed. He has no one to tell him no, no one to share the weight, no one to catch the drift before it becomes a fall. The single leader is a single point of failure, and when he fails, the whole church fails with him, because everything was resting on him alone. Plurality spreads the weight so that no one man carries what no one man should.

It protects the church too. A plurality can resist the bad idea, balance the blind spot, restrain the strong personality who would otherwise have his way unchecked. And it protects the elders from each other, because a body of men submitted to one another and to Scripture can correct the one among them who begins to wander, including the pastor, who is one elder among elders and not a tier above them. The lead pastor who refuses real plurality, who keeps a board he controls rather than a fellowship he submits to, has rejected the protection God built for his own soul.

sections.title: How a Plurality Actually Functions
sections.body:
Plurality on paper is not plurality in practice, and I have seen churches with five elders run entirely by one. So make it real, concretely.

Decide important things together and live with what the room decides, even when it is not what you wanted. If the pastor always gets his way, you do not have elders, you have an audience. Real plurality means the lead man loses sometimes, submits sometimes, defers to the judgment of the body, and a pastor who cannot lose a vote among his own elders is not leading a plurality. He is performing one.

Guard one another's lives, not only the church's business. Elders meetings that are only logistics have missed the point. Ask one another the hard questions. How is your marriage. How is your prayer. Where are you tempted. A plurality that watches over the church but never watches over its own members is a board, not a body, and it will lose a man to a hidden sin no one was close enough to see.

Share the shepherding. Divide the flock so that every member is genuinely known by an elder, visited, prayed for, pursued when they drift. The office is not a meeting. It is a labor, and the meeting exists to serve the labor, never to replace it.

sections.title: Men Who Will Give an Account
sections.body:
Peter, writing to elders, calls himself a fellow elder, and then he says shepherd the flock of God that is among you, not under compulsion but willingly, not for shameful gain but eagerly, not domineering but being examples. And then the line that should sober every man who takes the office. You will give an account.

The flock is not yours. The sheep belong to the Chief Shepherd, and you are an under-shepherd, holding them in trust, and one day you will stand before the owner and account for how you handled what was his. That is the weight of the office, and it is why the office cannot be given to the merely impressive. The impressive man will give an account of his impressiveness. The faithful man will give an account of his faithfulness. Only one of those accounts will stand.

So if you are an elder, or asked to be one, do not measure yourself by the size of the church or the success of the programs. Measure yourself by the sheep. Are they known. Are they fed. Are they guarded. Did you go after the one that wandered, or did you let it go because it was inconvenient.

The Chief Shepherd is coming. He will ask about the sheep, not the org chart. Lead like a man who believes that.
